doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Henry Mancini and the limits of jazz scores
summary: Mandel calls Mancini the ideal film and pops composer, and says jazz or rock scores each fit only a small fraction of movies.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Well, it’s growing and I’m happy to hear you say that. Hank Mancini is – left very big shoes to fill though, I’ll tell you that. He was my ideal of what the perfect composer was for films for pops, for almost anything. He was so elegant in everything he did; he did it right and on top of it he was a marvelous human being.
He did everything he did with a lot of class.
Oh he had class, indeed he did.
And I guess his success with, Peter Gunn and Mr. Lucky, really opened the door for a lot of writers in Hollywood.
It sure did. It sure did. For a while there they were trying to put jazz scores to everything and it was quite laughable.

Because jazz scores fit a very tiny fraction of the movies that people tried to put – rock ‘n’ roll really fits a very tiny fraction too. More of the pictures now are conducive to rock ‘n’ roll, you see a piece of film like, Pulp Fiction, and I couldn’t envision using anything but rock ‘n’ roll in that thing.
